parsed_response.reasoning: The diff shows `minimumTokenResponseSchema = z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Since ZodType has no toString override, both computed keys evaluate to the literal "[object Object]" — the second overwrites the first, so the schema is effectively `{access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown.optional}`. Zod strips unknown keys by default, so in sharing mode `refreshTokenResponse.data` contains only access_token, meaning `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is always undefined (the placeholder branch always fires) and expiry fields are dropped from the credential updated in e.g. Office365CalendarService (`o365AuthCredentials = {...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)}` loses expiry). The mechanism is verifiable directly from the added file. This is a real correctness defect in the new shared parsing logic.

judged_text: The computed keys `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" (ZodType has no toString override), so the schema is effectively `{access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown}` — the duplicate key overwrites the `z.number()` catch-all and the stated 'any property with a number is the expiry' behavior does not exist. In sharing mode every refresh response is parsed down to `{access_token}` alone because zod strips unknown keys — expiry_date/expires_in and refresh_token are silently dropped from every synced token, so persisted credentials never get a new expiry (perpetual refresh churn) and the placeholder refresh_token branch always fires; the sync feature's core data contract is not implemented.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the object schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Since `z.string()` returns an object and Zod types don’t override `toString()`, both keys evaluate to the literal string `"[object Object]"`, and the second one overwrites the first. The resulting schema is effectively `{ access_token: z.string(), "[object Object]": z.unknown().optional() }`, so it does not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” behavior, nor does it preserve `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`refresh_token` in sharing mode (Zod will strip unknown keys by default). This makes the parsing/contract incorrect in the added sharing-mode token refresh path.
